biography:
Wagner Ebrahim, a name now synonymous with Brazilian flair on the track, didn't inherit his passion for racing; he discovered it. Growing up in the bustling favelas of São Paulo, Wagner's first taste of speed came from navigating the chaotic streets on a battered scooter, a skill he honed out of necessity. One sweltering afternoon, while delivering groceries, he stumbled upon a local karting track. Captivated, he spent hours watching seasoned racers, his eyes gleaming with a hunger only speed could satisfy. He convinced the track owner to let him drive an old kart, and the rest, as they say, is history. 

Wagner swiftly rose through the ranks, trading his scooter for a racing suit. His raw talent and sheer determination caught the attention of Ginetta, offering him a spot in their junior program. Ebrahim's debut was nothing short of spectacular, showcasing his natural speed and aggressive overtaking style. He secured multiple podium finishes, establishing himself as a rising star. 

Despite facing numerous challenges, including funding issues and fierce competition, Wagner persevered. A defining moment came during the Brazilian GT Championship, where he battled neck-and-neck with veteran racer Ricardo Silva, ultimately snatching victory on the final lap. This win solidified his reputation and secured him a spot on the international stage. Now at 24, Wagner is at the peak of his career, racing with Ginetta and constantly pushing the limits, chasing his ultimate dream of one day competing in Formula 1.
drivingStyle: Ebrahim's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks in corners, often pushing the limits of adhesion. While some criticize his aggressive approach, his tire management is surprisingly astute. He conserves his tires early in the race, allowing him to unleash a blistering pace in the closing laps. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Silva
rivalries.reason: A veteran Brazilian racer, Silva initially dismissed Ebrahim as an upstart. Their intense on-track battles and contrasting driving styles created a fierce rivalry that captivated fans.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Rossi
rivalries.reason: Rossi is a fiercely competitive Italian driver known for her tactical racing. She and Ebrahim have clashed multiple times, with their rivalry fueled by differing opinions on racing ethics and fair play.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka, a stoic Japanese driver, represents the epitome of precision and control. Ebrahim's flashy style directly contrasts Tanaka's methodical approach, leading to several heated moments on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears a lucky bracelet made of intertwined race car tires.
Listens to Brazilian Samba music at deafening volume 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to use the number 13, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Life's too short to drive slow. If you ain't risking it, you ain't living it."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian GT Championship in 2022 after an epic last-lap overtake against veteran Ricardo Silva, proving his dominance on home soil.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2021 Ginetta Supercup race at Silverstone due to a mechanical failure, costing him valuable championship points and shaking his confidence.
